Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Continue from origin/handoff/r10-sav-comfort 50f27375 (body 420c0e99); do not restart from main. Implement the five carries on top, including the owner baseline spec and card-tab equality, with the flat-price null control.

Owns two limits R10-SAV-BASELINE (#2255, PR #2411) left open in the savings figures. (1) The month row's comfort-matched null: the flat-price null must separate comfort, COP timing and stored heat, not be driven to 0. (2) The summer_dhw_only start-bound limit: the start-of-horizon settlement is capped by the thermostat's space-heat cost, which leaves summer_dhw_only negative. Seams: optimizer.py and ledger.py. The acceptance is the carried comfort text from R10-SAV-BASELINE, which you re-measure at your merge base. Part of #201.

Carried findings (roster origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster, all owed in this PR):

[carry 1] From R10-SAV-BASELINE (#2255, PR #2411): the month row's flat-price null reads 10.83 % saved at that head (43.66 % at its base) by `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_baseline.py`. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_null_terms.py` splits the 13.9 kWh gap (booked thermostat 128.4, plan 114.5) into three terms, and the acceptance must separate them, not drive the null to 0. (a) Comfort: 6.6 kWh, about 5 of the 10.83 points; the plan holds 18.79 °C against a 20.44 °C mean target; a comfort-matched baseline or a priced comfort shortfall answers it. (b) COP timing: power-weighted COP +17.27 % at a flat price, because the plan heats in the warmer hours; this is a real saving and must survive. (c) Stored heat: +23.7 kWh_th (about 13.3 kWh_e) left unsettled by the 2-day window; the month row does not settle it, `predicted_savings` does. Control: the harness's `const` arm (outdoor at the window mean) reads timing +0.00 % and gap 15.6 = comfort 5.1 + start drawdown 10.1. Acceptance: with comfort matched, the `const` arm with stored heat settled at both ends (or a window long enough) reads about 0, and the varying-outdoor arm reads the timing term, not 0. Second limit: the start-of-horizon settlement is capped by the thermostat's space-heat cost, and that leaves `summer_dhw_only` at -12.74 % predicted savings (-3.17 % on main; -0.27 SEK on a 2.09 SEK reference), because the summer house starts above the end's comfort caps. Settled at the caps alone it read 1.95 %, but `away_setback` then read 60.71 %. Re-measure both at your merge base.

[carry 2] From the D15 production triage of the owner's 7.0.4 diagnostics bundle (2026-10-24; derived ratios only, the bundle stays out of every ref): the open month's savings are negative by volume, not by price timing. The booked thermostat baseline (`add_savings_settlement`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/ledger.py:195-228, fed by `current_action["baseline_kw"]` from optimizer.py:5689) is a modelled electric kWh, while `savings_actual` is metered kWh (spot plus immersion); the month's baseline kWh is 0.384x its metered kWh, and the plan's own prediction under-reads the meter 1.56x over the 192-sample accuracy window, 17.8 % of metered draw falling in intervals the plan predicted at zero (pump-initiated hot water). Flat-price null: pricing both sides at one price leaves 95-102 % of the negative month (volume term -94.5 %, timing term -5.5 %), so the owner-required null "savings about 0 on a flat-price profile" fails on volume before any comfort or stored-heat separation is reached. The baseline and the actual must be compared on one basis: both modelled, or the baseline scaled by the same meter calibration (`accuracy.power_ratio`), with draw the plan never commanded classified rather than charged to the plan. Controls: the flat-price null reads about 0 on a synthetic install whose meter exceeds the model by a fixed factor; a no-gap install keeps today's figures byte-identical; one mutant. Harness shape: recompute volume and timing terms from `ledger.months[<month>].lines` (synthetic bundle only in-tree).

[carry 3] Correction to the D15 triage carry on savings volume (2026-10-24; derived ratios only). The earlier text called the draw in plan-zero intervals "pump-initiated hot water". That is wrong: the integration owns the mode. The cause is the integration's own DHW handling. Re-derived from the 57-step pump-duty ledger (`pump_arbiter._observe`/`_verdict`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py:1001-1038): 3 of 4 planned one-step DHW slots show no run inside the slot, and 7 of 8 plan-idle steps within three steps after a slot ran. Null control: plan-idle steps with no DHW slot in the previous three steps ran 4 of 41, and 3 of those 4 continue one DHW run. Seam: an idle row writes no mode (`desired`, pump_arbiter.py:700-707), so the DHW mode written for the slot stays on through the idle steps. The pump then starts late and charges to its own set-point, while the plan booked one 15-minute slot. Over the 192 accuracy rows: 10 of the 13 running rows in plan-zero intervals sit next to a planned-on step, which is start and run-on lag. The plan's kW for its own commanded steps reads 1.28x low, because the arbiter commands a flow set-point and not a kW. Standby is refuted (median 0.0 kW in idle rows). Immersion (3.9 % of the month's actual kWh) is in `savings_actual` (ledger.py:225) but has no counterpart in the thermostat baseline. Owner acceptance (binding on this group): the corrected monthly savings must equal what the card's Savings tab shows. Today the card reads `MonthlySavingsSensor.extra_state_attributes["savings_months"]` (sensor.py:487-525, card `_savingsPageHtml`), which is `ledger.savings_months` (coordinator.py:7864, ledger.py:332). Main's code over the bundle's ledger store gives a Savings cell equal to the sensor's state, by construction. The divergences the owner sees are in the same tab and header. (a) The header's "Projected savings" (`_plan_predicted_savings`, a plan-horizon figure) is positive while the month row is negative. (b) The row's Baseline and Actual columns are on a bill basis (capacity, wear and immersion, ledger.py:302 `month_cost`), while its Savings cell is a spot-energy difference. So Baseline is 3.49x the thermostat's booked cost, and the % column divides one basis by the other. Fix in `ledger.savings_months` only, so that the tab, the sensor state and the closed-month receipt's saved line read one figure on one basis. Pin it with a test that renders the card's Savings page from the sensor payload and asserts each cell equals `ledger.savings_months`.

[carry 4] Owner specification for the savings baseline (tvofi, 2026-10-24, binding acceptance criterion). Actual consumption is calculated from the heat pump's power sensor. The baseline must use power levels similar to the ones recorded, simulated as a plain thermostat over the exact same price profile, for both space heating and DHW. The DHW baseline assumes the DHW thermostat is always on: no DHW windows. Savings are the cost of that baseline minus the metered actual cost, priced over the same profile. Under one flat price, the volume difference may remain, but timing savings must be 0. The card's Savings tab equals ledger.savings_months cell for cell. Replace the modelled-thermostat volume (_thermostat_held_state, optimizer.py:358; baseline at 0.38x metered) with this definition.

[carry 5] Correction to carry-d15-sav-volume-2 (D15 triage, 2026-10-24; derived ratios only). Withdrawn: "an idle row writes no mode, so the DHW mode keeps the pump charging through plan-idle steps". The owner's integration also owns the supply switch, and the ledger statistic it rested on, 7 of 8 idle steps after a DHW slot ran, is not evidence that the pump ran outside a planned slot. Three seams. (1) The ledger freezes `planned` at the step's first one-minute tick (`_observe`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py:1006-1010). That is the plan from before the mid-step re-solve, and the re-solve can move a DHW slot onto the current step. In the bundle, the 13:00 row reads planned dhw while the 13:13 solve's action for that same step is space 0.5 kW and dhw 0. `ran` is real metered pump draw of at least `on_threshold_kw` (0.25 kW) on any one-minute pass (pump_arbiter.py:1013-1015). `dhw` is the mode flag or a tank rise (pump_arbiter.py:1020-1026). (2) The arbiter never writes the switch (pump_arbiter.py:46). The switch is written once per coordinator cycle, from the new plan's step 0 (`_apply_action`, coordinator.py:7581-7595, after the solve at :5634). Cycles run every 15.39 min (median of 641) against 15-minute steps, at a phase spread uniformly through the step (quartiles 4.3, 8.2 and 11.4 min). So each switch-on lasts into the next step, and a slot written late in its own step starts the compressor in the following one: 3 of 4 planned DHW slots show no run in-slot. (3) Checked and refuted: the solve's switch schedule disagreeing with its ask. 0 of 672 published steps were switched on without an ask, or off with one. The bundle holds no switch-state history, so "switch commanded off while draw continued" can be neither confirmed nor ruled out. Owed: score each ledger step against the plan in force when the step's actuation happened (re-freeze `planned` at each cycle's adoption), and actuate the switch at step boundaries, from the arbiter's one-minute tick, rather than at the cycle phase. Controls: a synthetic install with the cycle phase at 0 and at 14 min books identical duty verdicts; a step whose plan changed mid-step is scored against the plan that actuated it; one mutant per seam. The card-equality acceptance from carry-d15-sav-volume-2 stands.
